cases.description: Assign a non‑null Resolver implementation and verify that getResolver() returns an Optional containing the same instance.
Assign null to the resolver; the method should store null and getResolver() must return an empty Optional.
Set a resolver, then set a different resolver and verify that the second value overwrites the first (the latest resolver is returned).

cases.expected: Optional.of(DummyResolver) for messageA, Optional.empty() for messageB
cases.description: Create two Message instances; setResolver on only one of them and confirm that the other instance remains unaffected (its resolver stays empty).
Assign a non‑null Resolver first, then assign null. The second call should clear the stored resolver, so getResolver() must return an empty Optional.
Set the same Resolver instance twice. The stored resolver should remain the same instance; getResolver() returns an Optional containing that instance.
Set a Resolver, then invoke unrelated Message methods (addRecord, toWire, getHeader). The resolver should stay unchanged, and getResolver() must still return the originally set Resolver.

Provide a Resolver implementation that extends the base Resolver class (CustomResolver). Verify that setResolver stores it correctly and getResolver() returns an Optional containing the subclass instance.

Set two different resolvers sequentially, then set null. The final state must be empty, confirming that null overwrites any previously stored resolver regardless of how many times setResolver was called.
